fieldMarks: 9.4-10.6 in; plump quail with a forward-curving black topknot.
White streaks on gray-brown sides and a heavily scaled pattern on the belly.
Call a loud 'chi-CA-go', the second note highest.
behavior: Lives in coveys most of the year; often seen strutting across clearings, nodding at each step, and flushes in fast, low, whirring flight.
Forages on the ground by scratching and picking; eats mainly seeds and leaves, also acorns, berries, bulbs and insects.
Permanent resident; comes into well-covered yards and parks for grain or birdseed.
habitat: Broken chaparral, woodland edges, coastal scrub, open oak woodland and streamside growth; also suburbs, farms, pinyon-juniper and grassland edges.
Avoids mountains; introduced birds farther inland use other brushy habitats.
range: A permanent resident of the Pacific coast states and parts of the interior West; common along the California coast and present in the Northwest, Rocky Mountain and Southwest regions, including introduced populations.

lookalikes.name: Gambel's quail
lookalikes.howToTell: Replaces California quail in desert country; compare carefully where ranges meet.

lookalikes.name: Mountain quail
lookalikes.howToTell: Mountain quail lives mostly at higher elevations and has broad white bars on reddish sides.
